Ghost Launches Core: Personal AI Computer Runs Locally on Powerful Hardware  
  
San Francisco-based startup Ghost has emerged from stealth with $11 million in funding and launched Core, a screenless personal AI computer designed for fully on-device processing. The device pairs an NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 GPU with an AMD Ryzen CPU, 64 GB of RAM, and a 1 TB SSD, priced at $3,499.Core runs AI models locally, encrypts personal data, and builds contextual awareness from a user’s apps and files without requiring cloud subscriptions. The company positions the product as a privacy-first alternative to subscription-based AI services.Early demand has been robust: Batch 1 sold out quickly, and interest remains open for Batch 2.

   A new startup has built an AI PC which has sold out of its first batch
   Ghost's Core is a 'personal AI computer that runs models entirely on device'
   It connects to your apps, services and devices, so it 'builds context on your life over time, and works continuously to help you'

  

Ghost is a startup in the AI field that wants to capitalize on the desire to have agents running locally rather than using AI in the cloud — and to get this done with a minimum of fuss.

TechCrunch reports that Ghost's first product is a PC for using local AI agents which runs those LLMs (Large Language Models) exclusively on-device, ensuring your data stays private (I'll come back to that point later). [...] As well as the ease of use, privacy is the other big selling point for Core. It's tapping into a market of the increasing number of people realizing the potential of AI for helping with their life or work, who are concerned about sending their thoughts or data into the cloud, when they have no real idea where those queries or uploads will end up.

Core will run your AI agents continuously taking on whatever tasks you require while keeping all your data on the device, with Ghost promising that it's not going anywhere else. The personal data on the PC is encrypted to keep it safe — even Ghost can't access the data — and the device is specifically designed to keep running even if Ghost were to shut down (there's no subscription fee here). [...] This is for the AI enthusiast who doesn't want to buy a Mac mini (or Mac Studio) with maxed-out memory (required for larger AI models), and then have to mess around setting up everything themselves.

Javaid stresses that the PC comes with software built specifically for running those pre-installed AIs, avoiding all the fuss of model configuration. The CEO observes: "You can run [AI] models on existing hardware, but it's a terrible experience on many levels."

Core updates its models automatically as new upgrades emerge (unless you don't want that to happen), and the idea is that it's a seamless system and "similar to how Tesla works" with over-the-air updates.

Ghost AI CEO Zain Javaid, 19, just introduced Core, a $3,499 personal AI computer designed to run AI models locally 24/7.  
  
Core runs entirely on device, with an NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell GPU, 64GB of RAM, 1TB storage, and an AMD Ryzen 5 7600 CPU. The goal is to let AI work with your files, apps, wearables, and other devices without sending that data to the cloud.  
  
The bigger idea is personal AI that you actually own. Instead of renting access to AI through a cloud service, Core is designed to keep the models and your data inside your home while letting agents handle tasks in the background.

Ghost has officially unveiled Core, a screenless personal AI computer designed to run AI models and agents locally on dedicated hardware. The device includes an NVIDIA RTX Pro 4000 SFF Blackwell GPU and is designed to connect with apps, files, wearables and smart-home devices while continuously running AI tasks.   
  
Core is priced at $3,499, with the first batch scheduled to ship in late October. Ghost also announced an $11 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz. These capabilities and privacy claims are primarily company claims and have not been independently benchmarked by us.
